entries.rationale: The classical definition and distributional characterization are needed before complex rigidity.
Canonical representatives and uniqueness are proved, rather than imported through GZ.
Preserve the source line-test definition and prove the PSHD redundancy beside it.
The connected zero-dimensional case is explicitly finite constant; no positive-dimensional argument is applied to it.
In one complex dimension the line test is the subharmonic definition.
Complex Hessian positivity, canonical regularization and uniqueness are internally proved.
Retain the identically-minus-infinity alternative before applying local integrability.
The annulus comparison proves logarithmic radial supremum convexity used for Lelong slopes.
Translation-invariant subharmonicity gives real convexity; the strip use is explicit.
Coordinate independence follows from the internal pullback theorem.
Domain and manifold definitions agree by the proved coordinate-change pullback.
Componentwise membership and the empty-domain singleton follow from the local definition; no separate theorem is imported.
General manifold pullback follows in coordinate charts, retaining the collapse alternative.
Local canonical representatives patch uniquely on charts.
Local versus global poles are distinguished before globalization.
The Euclidean globalization is proved through capacity, not imported.
The arbitrary compact complex, possibly non-Kahler, theorem has a complete Hermitian proof.
All finite local exponents are supplied, with disc and polydisc estimates.
Arbitrary directed decreasing limits and upper envelopes are handled without a cofinal-sequence assumption.
Countable envelope selection is proved from second countability.
Local integrability makes pole sets Lebesgue null.
The required complex pluripolar discrepancy is proved after capacity, beyond the earlier real-polar version.
Pointwise canonical determination and the non-pluripolar density refinement are available.
Weighted pole sums/globalization give countable-union closure in the applicable local and compact settings.
L1 limits have canonical psh representatives; tail envelopes and discrepancy supply the quasi-everywhere limsup passage.
Both bounded-above extension and the unbounded codimension-two case are covered; Hausdorff slicing repairs the projection gap.
The noncollapsed invariant infimum is proved, with the product-strip interface actually used by Part I.
Invariant exhaustion plus internally proved pseudoconvex sublevels/products supplies the cited minimum principle.
The weak upper-bound seam condition and exceptional poles are handled locally.
Boundary max-pasting is an exact specialization of the internal gluing proof.
Part I uses coordinate balls via bal_general. The complete ball Perron replacement is internal; the broader strongly pseudoconvex/discontinuous-boundary formulation is not imported.
Local bounded comparison and domination, including boundary limits, are proved in the product foundation.
Only the topology needed for product locality is introduced.
Local quadratic psh tests give ordinary-open inclusion; the local base also gives compatibility.
Superlevel openness follows from truncation and the topology definition.
The source plurithinness vocabulary is left there; the prequel obtains its needed neighborhood base directly.
The complete native thin-witness normalization is not needed by the direct local-base proof.
The complete source global plurithin witness has no retained caller; its former duplicate was removed.
Native finite-union thinness is bypassed by the direct finite-test base construction.
The source Cartan characterization is not used as an external input to the prequel base/locality proof.
The local base is needed for product locality and is proved by a simpler finite-test construction.
The cited non-Borel counterexample remains in SGPT; the book uses completed measures and proves the quasi-Lindelof interface it needs.
Coordinate/domain compatibility is a consequence of the local base proof.
The short compact-neighborhood corollary is fully proved in SGPT; its usc/base prerequisites are internal.
The complete source continuity proof uses only the supplied pullback and base foundation.
Manifold charts use the already proved coordinate-independent local base.
Smooth-background changes and finite-locus continuity are internally established.
Strict difference sets, including a pole of the lower function, are covered.
Every nonempty plurifine open set has positive volume; polar sets cannot contain one.
Removing common poles and additional pluripolar sets preserves the finite-locus extrema.
Quasi-extrema fix undefined differences at common poles.
The normalized radial slope and spherical mean/current identity are both supplied.
The book fixes Lelong(log|z|^2)=1 and dd^c=i partial-barpartial/(2pi).
The growth reformulation and normalized current/spherical identity are proved.
Analyticity of all positive Lelong level sets is proved from multiplier coherence and local estimates.
Addition uses spherical means and linearity, repairing the source's supremum-slope shortcut; maxima/scaling follow separately.
Upper-envelope Lelong infima are proved with exact local upper bounds and L1 convergence.
Generic minima are attained and constant off a proper analytic exceptional set.
Smooth-model divisorial Lelong numbers and model independence are supplied, including the required divisor realization.
The weight is exp(-phi); stalk and sheaf conventions are explicit.
The one-variable threshold checks the normalization without silently doubling the weight.
The unlabelled Nadel proposition is fully proved using internal L2 and analytic algebra.
Tensor-product extension and diagonal restriction prove subadditivity internally.
Normalized asymptotic ideal order recovers divisorial Lelong numbers, with finite discrepancy errors.
The point-blowup divisor recovers the original point Lelong number.
The general uniform strict valuation criterion and finite-resolution case include strict transforms, not merely exceptional divisors.
The source increasing-stalk stability and strong openness are both proved, without importing them.
Submersion equality follows locally from product Fubini and the internal restriction estimate.
Restriction means the image ideal, distinguished from the sheaf tensor pullback.
The local extension estimate and iterated-coordinate restriction give the source submanifold ideal inclusion.
Smooth local backgrounds exist internally and define the exact theta-psh convention.
Compact bounded-difference singularity preorder is explicitly distinguished from local inequalities.
Local psh results pass through fixed smooth backgrounds; the global uses receive explicit proofs.
Compact normalized intervals and supremum continuity are proved, including moving-point Hartogs bounds.
Normalization on a closed non-pluripolar set has the needed upper-bound/compactness consequence.
The decreasing net has a noncollapsed limit and actual net L1/supremum convergence.
On a fixed smooth divisor model, pullback L1 continuity and normalized compactness give upper semicontinuity and a uniform divisorial bound; local proper-model continuity is explicit.
Smooth-target psh descent/pullback is fully proved; unused general singular-space FN is excluded.
The background is removed by a local smooth potential; the actual ball replacement is canonical and complete.
Local rational types are defined; a common global rational ideal type is asserted only on compact X.
Rational scaling, sums and maxima clear common degrees; a general noncompact common denominator is not claimed.
Divisorial logarithmic types and bounded remainder are made explicit on smooth models.
Subtracting the divisor leaves bounded potentials; internal regularization gives nefness and the strict Kahler conclusion.
Composition pulls back coherent generators and preserves bounded remainders and rational coefficients.
Resolution means an SNC total divisor, including strict transforms.
Exactly EI-RES principalization is accepted; its rational logarithmic consequence is derived internally.
Decreasing approximants, vanishing curvature errors and two-scale multiplier inclusions are separate conditions.
All three gentle conditions and the Kahler smooth model are explicit.
The decreasing dyadic construction, exact ideal types and two-scale inclusions have a complete proof after internal weighted L2 inputs.
Finite-resolution integrability-to-growth gives the actual comparison without a division theorem.
The ideal is defined by local bounded growth, distinct from integrability.
Finite jet/analytic algebra proves coherence; a proper-direct-image coherence theorem is not silently invoked.
The complete asymptotic inclusion is proved by finite discrepancies. Its sharper dimension-loss Briancon-Skoda statement is unused and not imported.
The strict positive Holder exponential extension has a full glued proof at the exact delegated scope.
Weak/strong positivity and order-zero consequences are established before products.
Pseudo-effectivity and bigness, including empty classes, use internally defined current cohomology.
Spaces of positive representatives use the internal current/cohomology interface.
Global smooth-background potentials and bounded-difference independence justify current singularity types.
The current/potential correspondence is supplied with its smooth-background independence.
The normalized divisor current has Lelong number one; no factor of two is introduced.
Pole sets are independent of smooth background changes.
The non-Kahler locus convention is included with the complete realization theorem.
Compact ideal stationarity and internal approximation produce one analytic Kahler current realizing the locus.
The non-nef locus and allowance identity have exact big/non-big conventions.
Positive residual subtraction and the countable divisorial decomposition are proved.
Divisorial and non-divisorial parts are defined after their existence.
The modified-nef definition, background independence and closed convex cone properties are proved.
Big-class minima and the pseudo-effective boundary limit agree in the exact stated scope.
Nef pullback and modified-nef pushforward follow from supplied smooth-background and divisor calculations.
Generic strict-transform equality uses the internal divisor-isomorphism locus, not an unproved general FN theorem.
Metrics are quadratic forms and singular fibers are handled with the source convention.
Tensor products multiply quadratic values and add potential weights.
Frame changes give the first Chern form with the fixed operator normalization.
The bundle identity follows from the proved local divisor formula.
The projective chart calculation checks unit total mass and the metric convention.
Pointwise psh weights define metrics, not merely an almost-everywhere curvature class.
The quadratic convention and smooth-reference change are explicit.
Tensor weights add; positivity and singular-fiber conventions follow from the definition.
The fully calculated native P1 logarithmic metric is left in SGPT with both foundational identities supplied.
Section-defined finite maxima use rational coefficients and quadratic norms.
Finite rational convex generation is proved by clearing degrees and multiplying sections.
The full uniform compact-submanifold norm estimate and tensor-power threshold are proved, with factorial volume conversion.
Leave the complete source type-comparison application in SGPT; supply its point estimate, weighted finite-section Hilbert/gentle-background interface and sufficient finite discrepancy bound.
